what_changed: North Carolina's State Board of Elections reports 1,101,321 ballots cast through Oct 21 (1,050,225 in-person early votes and 51,096 mail ballots), compared with 798,778 at the same point in 2022.
why_it_matters: North Carolina's official count can be compared with 2022 on a like-for-like basis; it reflects when people vote, not final turnout or who is ahead.

what_changed: Maricopa County Elections removed one early-ballot tabulator from use for the rest of the cycle after its digital counter displayed an error; its ballots from the prior two days were reconciled with the system log and will be re-run on another tabulator (county release, Oct 22).
why_it_matters: It shows the county's reconciliation step catching an equipment display error before results are released; no effect on ballots was reported.

what_changed: Friday, Oct 23 is the last day to request a ballot by mail (including a replacement) in Maricopa County.
why_it_matters: After today, a voter without a mail ballot votes in person at a vote center, early or on Election Day.

what_changed: Maricopa County states the signature cure deadline is 5:00 p.m. on Nov 8, 2026; the dashboard previously showed a derived date with no time.
why_it_matters: Voters contacted about a questioned signature have a firm cutoff to fix it.

what_changed: Maricopa County confirms ID Verify for the general election: show a photo ID at any vote center to mark an early ballot "ID Verified" and skip signature checks; on Election Day it can be tabulated on site.
why_it_matters: Drop-offs with ID can reach tabulation faster; Maricopa expects about 307,000 early ballots returned on the final weekend or Election Day.

what_changed: NBC News reports 20,622,633 early votes nationally (about 11.7M by mail, 9M in person) and 56.6M mail ballots requested or sent.
why_it_matters: Early totals depend on which states report and how; they do not show who is winning or what final turnout will be.

what_changed: Arizona Attorney General Kris Mayes and Secretary of State Adrian Fontes sued Maricopa County Recorder Justin Heap to restore regular ballots for 25 voters flagged as possible noncitizens; Heap says he is following state law on proof of citizenship.
why_it_matters: A court ruling could affect how flagged voters receive ballots before Nov 3.

what_changed: Maricopa County: about 320,000 early ballots returned as of Oct 20, vs about 270,000 at the same point in 2022 (County Recorder, rounded).
why_it_matters: More early returns so far than in 2022; earlier returns can mean earlier counting, not higher final turnout.

what_changed: Some Maricopa voters report not receiving mail ballots; county data show about 424 related contacts out of 1,988,858 mail voters, and USPS reports no local delays.
why_it_matters: Voters still without a ballot had until Oct 23 to request a replacement, or can vote in person.
